summary: This paper presents a co-design framework connecting frequency allocation in SNAIL-based tunable-coupler systems to fidelity-aware circuit transpilation, introducing an error budgeting model that captures both spectator-induced coherent errors and $T_1$-limited incoherent losses. The work demonstrates that frequency crowding fundamentally limits module size to ~4 qubits while achieving >0.99 fidelity, and develops FINESSE, a noise-aware transpiler that achieves 8.9% reduction in log-infidelity cost over SABRE on SNAIL architectures.
motivation: SNAIL-based tunable couplers enable flexible multi-qubit interactions but suffer from spectator-induced errors when qubits are tightly packed spectrally; balancing connectivity against fidelity degradation requires jointly optimizing hardware frequencies and circuit routing strategies.
method: An error budgeting approach quantifies spectator-induced infidelity as $\propto 2x_0/(x_1+\delta)^2$ and incoherent loss as $\propto x_0/(x_1+\delta)$ as functions of frequency detuning $\delta$. A constrained optimization using Nelder-Mead assigns qubit and SNAIL frequencies under realistic bounds (3.3–5.7 GHz qubits, 4.2–4.7 GHz SNAIL, 200 MHz minimum spacing); FINESSE extends SABRE/MIRAGE transpilation by replacing hop-count distances with fidelity-weighted shortest paths using $L_{ij}=-\log\max(C_{ij}, 10^{-10})$ and joint mirror-gate acceptance criteria.
result: Analysis shows gate fidelity is ~100× more sensitive to detuning for SNAIL-qubit conversion than qubit-qubit conversion; for $N=2,3,4,5$ qubits the geometric mean gate fidelities are 0.996, 0.994, 0.991, 0.940 respectively. On four-module SNAIL topologies, FINESSE achieves 8.9% log-infidelity reduction and 6.8% depth reduction versus SABRE; the 4-qubit 4-edge module provides optimal fidelity–connectivity tradeoff despite higher connectivity modules reducing routing overhead.
